subject: Renewal discussion: re-tiering & smoothing for 2028 commit
messages:
From: Olivia Bennett <olivia@zephyrai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: re-tiering & smoothing for 2028 commit

Hi Jonas,

Hope you had a good weekend. Our renewal with Redwood is up in Q4 and we want to talk about re-tiering the commit and smoothing the per-token pricing to avoid the big step functions we hit last year. Usage growth was higher-than-forecast and that caused us to exceed the top-of-tier ceiling; finance pushed back on the overage.

High-level ask: can Redwood propose a renewal structure that: 1) right-sizes our committed spend to match forecasted trajectory with a modest uplift cap (<=15%), 2) introduces per-token smoothing bands so unit price doesn't jump more than X% between slabs, and 3) allows a one-time mid-year true-up instead of monthly true-ups.

I attached our internal forecast (simple) and would like to schedule a 30-min sync next week to review suggested billing mechanics. Can you also confirm whether a phased uplift (quarterly) is possible under Dedicated vs Hosted pricing?

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Bennett
Head of Platform & Partnerships
ZephyrAI

Attachments: Zephyr_MAPlan_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Bennett <olivia@zephyrai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: re-tiering & smoothing for 2028 commit

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. Read-through looks good.

We can absolutely do a renewal path that reduces discontinuities between tiers. A couple of quick points we will propose on the formal MA:
- Right-size: we’ll model a 12-month staged commit with a 10–15% annual uplift cap and an optional step-up clause tied to usage triggers.
- Per-token smoothing: propose slab smoothing (3 bands) where unit price moves smoothly via interpolation rather than discrete jumps; we can set a maximum band jump of 8–12%.
- True-up cadence: we support a one-time mid-year true-up (preferred) for Hosted customers; Dedicated customers often prefer quarterly true-ups for allocation reasons, but we can make an exception with committed buffer.

I’m attaching a draft pricing proposal for you to review. Can we do Tue 6/1 10:00 PT for a 30-min walk-through? If that works, I’ll loop in Laura from finance for the billing mechanics details.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Jonas / Karthik — forwarding Olivia's note and your draft. Quick internal notes before the sync: 

1) Margin guardrails: We should include a minimum per-token floor in the MA so smoothing doesn't erode unit economics if usage drops. Suggest language: "floor equal to 80% of current blended rate".
2) Uplift cap: 10% feels safer from a renewals book perspective; 15% acceptable if we get a stronger commit term (24 months).
3) True-up: agree a one-time mid-year true-up for hosted is simpler. For Dedicated we can offer mid-year true-up but require a 5% buffer to ensure capacity reservation.

I'll be on the sync and can talk headcount/CS handoffs as part of renewal enablement.

-M

Jonas / Marissa — notes from the call (recap for thread):

- Agreed on a staged-commit structure: 4 quarters with an initial baseline commit covering 70% of FY forecast and two conditional step-ups (Q2 and Q4) that are customer-triggered if usage crosses defined thresholds.
- Per-token smoothing: implement 3 bands with linear interpolation between band boundaries. Max band jump capped at 10%.
- Uplift cap: 10% on annualized committed spend for a 12-month term; 12–15% considered only for 24-month commitment.
- True-up: Zephyr prefers a single mid-year true-up; we will offer that for Hosted. For Dedicated we require a 5% buffer or quarterly true-ups.

Next actions: Jonas to send redlined MA with these clauses + Laura to confirm invoice timing and when we can apply credits. I’ll draft clause text for smoothing and floor.

-Karthik

Hi Olivia — looping in official billing mechanics.

1) Invoice flow for mid-year true-up: we will issue a single adjustment invoice that applies credits or charges for the delta between committed and actual usage for the six-month period. That invoice posts to the next billing cycle and can be netted on a single statement (no multiple small credit notes).
2) Example pricing table: attached is a worked example using the forecast you provided. It shows $/1k-token at low/medium/high bands and the interpolation math.
3) Contracts: Jonas will send the redline. If you decide to shift to a 24-month commitment for a lower blended unit price, we will include a hard cap on annual increases in the MA.

Please see attached: redlined_MA_Zephyr_v1.pdf (contract redline) and pricing_example_Zephyr.xlsx. Let us know if you'd like a brief (15-min) finance-only rundown.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
